# Interface Components: VideoCanvas

## Interface Components: VideoCanvas

`window.InterfaceComponents.VideoCanvas` provides tracked bounding boxes and time-range activity labels over one video. It owns playback, frame stepping, keyframe interpolation, and hotkeys. Canonical annotation state stays in the Screen's controlled props.

Props: `src`, `frameRate`, `regions`, `selectedRegionIds`, `onAddRegion`, `onUpdateRegion`, `onDeleteRegion`, `onSelectRegion(id | null, { additive })`, `activeLabels`, `activeTimelineLabels`, `labelColors`, `fromName`, `toName`, `timelineFromName`, `enableTimelineLabels`, `activeTool` ("select" | "rectangle") + `onToolChange`, `showTimeline`, `showObjectTimeline`, `showActivityTimeline`, `showToolbar`, `showLayers` (default false; shell Outliner owns the region list; a user-requested Screen list uses RegionList), `playbackRates`, `onTimeUpdate(time, duration)`, `onFrameUpdate(frame)`, `syncGroup` + `syncOffset`, `minZoom` / `maxZoom`, `readOnly`, `hotkeys`.

### Two timelines under the video

- `VideoCanvas.ObjectTimeline` shows one row per tracked bounding box, its active lifespans, and its keyframes. Selecting a track selects its shape on the video. `showObjectTimeline` defaults to true.
- `VideoCanvas.ActivityTimeline` shows labeled time ranges independently of object tracks. `enableTimelineLabels` enables creating ranges; `showActivityTimeline` defaults to true when creation is enabled or imported `timelinelabels` regions exist. Ranges remain inspectable without enabling creation.
- `VideoCanvas.TimelineControls` controls the shared frame scale and horizontal position. Both panels stay aligned to the same playhead, timeline zoom, and scroll position, and each panel can collapse independently.
- `VideoCanvas.Timeline` remains the convenient wrapper for the shared controls and both panels. `showTimeline={false}` hides the timeline interface in the default layout. Use `showObjectTimeline={false}` for activity-only tasks and `showActivityTimeline={false}` for object-only tasks.
- `VideoCanvas.Timeline` supplies shared All / Objects / Activities tabs (initially All when both are available), filtered track counts, one toolbar, colored overview, shared ruler and a virtualized scroll surface. A chain button on dashed object-keyframe gaps connects only that interval in one guarded, undoable host edit, preserving endpoint geometry and the track’s Linear/Hold policy. Keyframes-only tracks must select Linear/Hold in Info first; incompatible topology is rejected. Brush gaps reuse the mounted MaskTools codec to materialize bounded pixel masks in one transaction; its opt-out, budgets, preserved gaps and stale-context cancellation apply. Generated masks fill presence without adding authored timeline diamonds. Selected object rows carry keyframe controls; activity bars show inclusive frame ranges. New activity creates an empty lane using the selected activity label. Double-click a lane twice to mark a range in that same lane; Enter on its focused label marks the playhead boundaries. Cancel/Escape discards a pending range. Lane creation and range creation are separate guarded host mutations. Switching tabs preserves the shared viewport and annotation state. Optional `headerActions` extends the header with Interface-owned actions without replacing its controls. Reuse this shell in screens and stories instead of private tabs or CSS overrides; `showObjects`/`showActivities` configure available families.
- `Timeline`, `ObjectTimeline` and `ActivityTimeline` accept `showEditors` (default false). Numeric editing belongs in `VideoCanvas.Info`; pass true only to opt into inline editors. Use root `showInfo` for a standalone default layout with Info; integrated shells render their InfoViewer. Rows, scrubbing, keyframe controls and activity-range dragging remain available with the existing read-only/lock guards. All object types use passive presence lines without drag/resize handles. Newly drawn boxes and vectors span the full video, with samples at frame 1 and the drawing frame. Vector keyframe controls add/remove samples and toggle visibility between keys. Mask keyframes copy/delete explicit painted frames without interpolation; interval visibility is disabled for masks. The final vector/mask sample is protected. This prop belongs to the compound timeline members, not the VideoCanvas root.
- `activeLabels` labels newly drawn objects; `activeTimelineLabels` labels newly created activity ranges. Bind these to separate LabelPicker selections. Omitting `activeTimelineLabels` falls back to `activeLabels` for existing Screens; passing an empty array explicitly creates unlabeled ranges.

Playback and precise editing:
- `VideoCanvas.FrameInput` seeks to a 1-based frame with Enter/blur; Escape cancels. `VideoCanvas.PlaybackControls` adds first/last, configurable `frameHop` steps and selected-activity looping. Alt+arrows hop; Home/End seek to limits.
- `playSelectionOnly` defaults to true: selected activity ranges define an inclusive playback envelope (gaps play). Playback starts within that range, stops on its last frame, or repeats with `loopSelection`. Supply `onLoopSelectionChange` for controlled loop state. No selection means full-video playback.
- `VideoCanvas.RangeEditor` edits selected activity start/end frames and displays inclusive duration. It supports individual imported ranges and respects locked/read-only regions.
- `VideoCanvas.Info` is a content-only selected-region editor. Spatial fields use native video pixels (fractional values supported), while rotation stays in degrees; all vertices/joints and interpolation choices are visible without a part dropdown. Pixel fields wait for native media dimensions and convert edits to the existing canonical percentage geometry; result formats are unchanged. It exposes current-frame rectangle geometry/keyframes, activity boundaries, vector coordinates/interpolation and track timing; mask dimensions and provenance are read-only. Omit `regionId` for a single selection or supply it for an individual InfoViewer row. It inherits the existing canvas controller, or accepts `controller` explicitly; `container` portals the same editor into a host Info mount point without creating a second canvas. Canvas and Info share validation, transactions and history. The production slot's `slotInstanceId` identifies the mounted editor for isolated portal routing; never key a shared target only by task ID or parse mutation revisions. Pass optional Interface-owned `TemporalInspector` children for domain attributes; the child context is scoped to the inspected region. Keep creation tools/playback/display settings outside Info and let the shell provide Lock/Hide/Delete. Unknown temporal versions, mismatched sources, read-only/locked tracks and missing atomic capability remain protected. See the `Components/VideoCanvas → In editor` Storybook preview for the real InterfaceEditorHarness/InfoViewer composition. This companion adds no result format or persistence service.
- `selectionPlaybackMode="disjoint"` skips gaps between selected activity ranges, playing each inclusive end frame for its full duration. The default remains `"envelope"`; clearing selection restores full-video playback.
- `VideoCanvas.TrackEditor` (or `showTrackEditor` in the default layout) previews split/join/reassign/copy/delete/append commands and applies one atomic host edit. Pass `mutationRevision={props.mutationRevision}`, `applyRegionTransaction={props.applyRegionTransaction}` and explicit `temporalSupport={{ versions: [1], resultTypes: ["videorectangle", "timelinelabels"] }}`. Supply `temporalBinding` (or `frameMetadata.binding`) to create fresh rectangles/activities with version-1 metadata. The editor offers an explicit legacy upgrade preview; reading never upgrades results. Repair/clipboard support vectors, masks and timestamp timebases with kind/dimension/policy compatibility guards. Never emulate the host callback with sequential edits. Missing capability, read-only, linking and unsupported tracks block edits with explanations. Choose a survivor for joins and explicit overwrite for occupied copy targets. Alt+T focuses the editor; Escape cancels a preview. Saving remains owned by the Interface.

- `VideoCanvas.FrameClipboard` copies an occupied frame through host `writeRegionClipboard`, then loads through `readRegionClipboard` (or a native paste event), previews a destination frame/range and applies one atomic host edit. Pass the existing callbacks along with the temporal transaction capability above. Use the root temporalBinding or frameMetadata.binding for source/item/timebase compatibility; a selected current-video temporal track is the fallback. Copy supports rectangles, vectors and masks. Whole tracks, incompatible sources, stale reads and protected destinations reject. Explicit overwrite is required for occupied destinations. Copy remains available read-only. The host's ordinary cut/duplicate/paste does not support temporal snapshots; use this panel for frame geometry. No component-level clipboard API or persistence is created.
- `VideoCanvas.TemporalInspector` takes `fields`, each with `schema: { name, scope: "static" | "temporal", required?, validate? }`, `label`, existing AnswerForm `kind`, `adapter: { toWidget, fromWidget }`, and `render`. Compose an existing ChoiceGroup/TextInput/etc. in the renderer and bind the provided `value/onChange/readOnly/missing/theme`; use `labelId` where the control supports it, otherwise supply an accessible label. Pass the temporal transaction capability above and supported version-1 metadata; do not use a second annotation store or the ordinary classification writer. Temporal edit scope is current frame, inclusive range, or forward fill; crossing gaps is explicit and never fills absent frames. Unset differs from false/zero/empty string. Static fields can be edited at absent frames. Expandable lanes edit authored blocks using pointer, keyboard and numeric create/resize/retime/delete operations. Set schema.forwardFill to "option" for independent checklist membership propagation; default "field" retains whole-value behavior. ObjectTimeline trims/retimes selected spatial spans and explicit keyframes atomically. Presence, interpolation policy and provenance are inspected separately from UI visibility. Host saving/history and ontology definition stay outside this component.
- Existing geometry, group transforms, keyframe/lifespan controls, activity gestures and numeric ranges route extended tracks through one atomic authoring plan. Mixed legacy/temporal groups are preflighted together, protected/invalid members reject the operation, and changes preserve temporal values outside removed occupancy. Geometry corrections stamp manual provenance while boundary samples retain their derivation. Legacy-only callbacks retain their previous contract. New track creation remains legacy unless a composing Interface supplies the explicit temporal contract.

- `VideoCanvas.MaskTools` takes `source` frame metadata, field bindings/labels, optional readable `frameProvider`, and width/height for new tracks. Sparse frame masks use exact LS RLE alpha bytes and a 64 MiB default decoded LRU cache; `cacheBudgetBytes` can lower that limit. A separate 64 MiB working-alpha budget bounds stroke/threshold/overlap allocations before fetching or decoding; `workingBudgetBytes` can lower it. Encoded payloads and browser video/RGBA surfaces are outside these two alpha budgets. Brush, erase and threshold edits are frame-scoped and apply one host transaction per stroke. Overlap policies are allow, exclude and overwrite (exclusive is a backward-compatible alias). Hidden/locked conflicts remain protected. Move, current-frame combine and RGB/HSV eyedropper thresholding are available. Explicit bounded signed-distance interpolation uses Preview/Apply or the timeline chain button, preserves authored/empty anchors and adds presence only inside the selected interval; it is not model tracking. Pixel-dependent thresholding requires a readable provider. Codec workers terminate on unmount/source changes. The Interface still owns Undo, saving and canonical regions.
- `VideoCanvas.GeometryTools` takes `binding, fromName, toName, labels` and optional `poseSchema: { jointIds, edges }`. Enable `videovector` explicitly in temporalSupport. Draw polygon/polyline vertices, drag ellipse bounds or place keypoints/skeleton joints; finish applies one host transaction. Handles and numeric fields edit the displayed frame. Insert/delete vertices, replace a single boundary, transform whole shapes and resize/rotate ellipses; invalid multipart/hole topology rejects. Reviewed bounded polygon resampling bridges differing vertex counts while preserving original samples and gaps. Stable vertex/joint IDs, missing and occluded joints, linear/hold/keyframe-only policies and unknown result metadata survive serialization. `videovector.value.sequence` contains `{frame, geometry}` samples plus versioned temporal metadata. Bounds follow allowDrawingOutside; read-only/stale/unsupported edits fail closed.
- `frameMetadata` accepts the successful value from `VideoCanvas.createFrameMetadataAdapter({binding,timestamps,pixelAccess})`. Timestamp starts are media-relative and the final frame ends at duration. With supplied metadata, seeks and selected playback use its intervals. The controller exposes requestedFrame, framePresentation and frameMetadataError; requestVideoFrameCallback observations distinguish the decoded frame from the requested destination. Browsers without that API use the media clock. Invalid metadata does not silently become CFR.
- `VideoCanvas.Suggestions` takes a host provider, taskId, source metadata, field bindings and labels. Discover/predict/progress/cancel/retry stay transient; point/box prompts and previews only mutate canonical results on explicit acceptance through one transaction. Manual frames are protected unless overwrite is explicitly enabled. Providers own ML, credentials and pixel extraction. Acceptance supports rectangles, vectors and exact-frame RLE masks on compatible CFR/timestamp sources. Mask outputs must match actual media dimensions; unknown outputs stay disabled. Optional createCodec supplies an owned mask preview codec. All model execution remains provider-owned.
- `VideoCanvas.ReviewMarkers` takes host `comments, sourceBinding, onFocusComment` and optional `referenceEditingSupported`. It navigates exact frame/range anchors and reports ambiguous/orphaned references. Anchor edits use the existing atomic host transaction; comment text, discussion and resolution stay in the existing Comments panel. The host must opt into temporal reference persistence on existing save callbacks.
- Share `regionFilter` and `timelineGroupBy` with the existing RegionList filter/group state. Filtering only changes visibility. RegionList.FilterControls and .TemporalSummary are controlled companions; density counts occupied tracks, not keyframes.
- The VideoCanvas chunk exports `VideoMultiView` (available as `window.InterfaceComponents.VideoMultiView` in the sandbox). Supply explicit view IDs, source/item/timebase bindings, offsets, activeViewId and controlled linked viewport state. Stable tiles share transport; only the active tile's timeline is shown. Set `layout="focus"` for one main editor and a right-hand column of clickable previews. Previews have no controls, are inert/read-only with hotkeys disabled, and activate through `onActiveViewChange` without remounting media. The default `layout="grid"` retains per-camera controls. renderViewCompanions(view, {active}) renders optional tools inside that tile context; binding, selection, callbacks, transactions and temporal clipboard are scoped to its source. It does not synthesize frame metadata. Cross-view association assigns entityId in one host transaction while keeping source-specific tracks distinct. Compose AudioCanvas/MediaTransport/passive transcript siblings with the same syncGroup; the media bus owns audio arbitration.

- `VideoCanvas.TimelineOverview` shows the full duration and a movable viewport window independent of the playhead. Drag its edges or use arrow keys on the start/end sliders to resize the visible interval without seeking. Optional `kind="object" | "activity"` filters the overview. Timeline controls include a follow-playhead toggle; dense keyframes are culled to the visible window.
- `defaultPlaybackRate`, `minPlaybackRate`, `maxPlaybackRate` configure initial speed and bounds; `playbackRates` supplies selector choices.
- `VideoCanvas.MediaStatus` provides loading/buffering/error feedback and retry. `onMediaError` and `onMediaRetry` let the Screen renew a source URL. The controller exposes media state for custom status UI.
- `allowDrawingOutside` defaults false and bounds creation/transforms. Multi-select rectangles to move/scale/rotate them together; group scaling is uniform to preserve rotated shapes. Batch keyframe/lifespan actions skip locked tracks.
- `showRegionLabels` defaults true; `showRegionScores` and `showRegionText` opt into additional overlays. Native-size viewing (Shift+2) is separate from fit (Shift+1).
- Sync groups coordinate buffering without losing the user's playback intent and choose one audible owner (audio preferred). `muted` remains the video's baseline preference.

Optional `VideoCanvas.ViewControls` supplies media-only brightness/contrast/saturation (0–200 percent), grid and selected-track isolation via `display/onDisplayChange`. It works read-only and does not change provider pixels or saved results.

`VideoCanvas.ZoomControls` accepts optional `compact` (default true) for an image-style percentage toolbar button with zoom steps, fit/native-size actions and 50/100/200/400% presets in an orientation-aware popover. Percentages remain relative to fitted view; native size remains a separate action. The default VideoCanvas layout uses a drawing rail beside the stage, zoom and display settings in the drawing rail, and playback below it. `VideoCanvas.Tools` owns the shared zoom/display controls; optional children replace only its creation tools, and `orientation="vertical"` selects a rail (default horizontal). Use this same shell for custom layouts instead of recreating its zoom/settings buttons. Pass optional `geometry` and `masks` configuration objects (the corresponding GeometryTools/MaskTools props) to Tools to include polygon, polyline, ellipse, keypoint, skeleton and mask paint/erase/move icons in the same rail. Supply poseSchema for skeleton creation. These companions render their overlays and share the root activeTool, so selection/rectangle hotkeys and tool switches cancel prior drafts. Activity creation stays in the timeline. New rectangles span the full video; timing is edited through keyframes. Polygon drawing shares ImageCanvas’s open cursor outline and closing-point highlight. The first point, double-click or Enter completes it, keeping polygon mode active for the next object. Completed polygons share ImageCanvas’s thin outline and fixed screen-size vertex handles. In Select mode, drag the body to move the whole polygon or a vertex to edit one point; each completed drag creates one current-frame edit through host history. Shapes and mask pixels use label colors, including CSS variables resolved in the canvas theme. Compact mask options match the image brush: source-pixel size, round/square tips, freehand/straight/polygon/lasso modes and a zoomed pixel grid. Painting reuses a selected mask only when its labels match; a different label creates a separate instance. The companions accept `toolbar` for this compact coordinated mode; standalone panels retain their original behavior. `VideoCanvas.ViewToolbar` is available for deliberately separate view controls; avoid duplicating it beside Tools. Reuse `VideoCanvas.Transport` for playback; Transport accepts optional children replacing its advanced navigation menu. It groups first/previous/play/next/last, time and frame/total, speed, selected-activity loop and fullscreen. Reuse `VideoCanvas.Stage` for a rounded dotted picture card with this transport; children replace its viewport area, `transportExtras` customizes advanced navigation, and `showTransport={false}` hides playback. `PlaybackControls compact` renders only frame hops for a custom menu. The horizontal `VideoCanvas.Toolbar` groups drawing/playback/view controls and includes a Display settings popover containing ViewControls. `useController().effectiveTheme` supplies the resolved light/dark theme for portals. FrameClipboard, TrackEditor, GeometryTools, MaskTools, Suggestions, ReviewMarkers and TemporalInspector supply their own shared panel/field/icon/preview presentation; compose them directly instead of duplicating their editing UI. TrackEditor chooses the command through its Track operation selector. Info shares these field styles while the host owns its surrounding chrome.


`VideoCanvas.KeyframeControls` renders previous / add-or-remove / next / hide-or-show span in rows and standalone compositions. The diamond plus/minus reflects whether the current frame already has a keyframe. The final crossed-eye / eye toggles presence from the preceding keyframe until the next via the existing lifespan action, not whole-region visibility. `compact` remains accepted for existing compositions.

Other compound members: `VideoCanvas.Root`, `.Viewport`, `.Toolbar`, `.PlayGroup`, `.TimeDisplay`, `.SpeedSelector`, `.KeyframeControls`, `.ZoomControls`, `.LayerManager`, `.RegionsOverlay`.

Video zoom is separate from timeline zoom: ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms the picture at the cursor; `mod+plus` / `mod+minus` / `shift+1` and `VideoCanvas.ZoomControls` control the video viewport. Alt- or middle-drag pans the picture; a selected box has a rotation handle (Shift snaps to 15°). Each range of a `timelinelabels` region is edited independently. With `syncGroup` the video shares transport state with AudioCanvas / TimeSeriesCanvas / MediaTransport and is muted while the group has an AudioCanvas.

Keyboard activity ranges (`enableTimelineLabels`): `shift+s` (`markSegmentStart`) marks the playhead frame as a range start and `shift+e` (`markSegmentEnd`) creates the range to the playhead (either order). The combined Timeline exposes Start/End buttons and a striped pending preview. The standalone ActivityTimeline creation lane does the same with Enter; Escape cancels a pending start. Seeking preserves the pending start while frame decoding temporarily disables End. Rebind through `hotkeys` like any other action.

Region `type` / `_value`:
- `videovector` — `{ sequence: [{frame, geometry}], framesCount, temporal }`; typed vectors, ellipses and stable joints, labels in `value.labels`.
- `videomasks` — sparse `{ frameMasks: { [frame]: LS_RLE_bytes }, original_width, original_height, format: "rle", framesCount, temporal }`. No raster interpolation; absent keys mean absent frames. Labels live in `value.labels`.
- `videorectangle` — `{ sequence: [{ frame, time, x, y, width, height, rotation, enabled }], framesCount, duration }` (frames are **1-based**, geometry in % of the frame, `enabled: false` ends a visible span). Label key: `value.labels`.
- `timelinelabels` — `{ ranges: [{ start, end }] }` (inclusive 1-based frames). Label key: `value.timelinelabels`.

Use the pure `fromVideoResults` and `toVideoResults` helpers to hydrate and save both result types without merging their labels or control names.
The helpers map a valid nonnegative safe-integer `item_index` to `_itemIndex`, including zero. A valid `_itemIndex` updates the saved binding; explicitly supplying `undefined` clears it. Omitting the property preserves the imported envelope. The host owns source reassignment and region scoping.

- **Pass shell state straight through.** `props.regions` already uses the canonical shape, so filter it to this canvas (`r._toName === TO_NAME`) and pass it as `regions`. Wire `selectedRegionIds={props.selectedRegionIds}`, `onAddRegion={props.addRegion}`, `onUpdateRegion={props.updateRegion}`, `onDeleteRegion={props.deleteRegion}`, `onSelectRegion={(id, opts) => props.selectRegion(id, opts)}` (a `null` id clears the selection).
- **Created regions are complete.** The canvas stamps `activeLabels` → `labels`, `labelColors` → `colors`, and `fromName`/`toName` → `_fromName`/`_toName`. Do not rebuild or re-id them in the screen. Always pass the same `labelColors` map you give the LabelPicker.
- **No Delete buttons in slots.** `onDeleteRegion` is for the canvas's own delete gestures. The shell already renders Lock / Hide / Delete around `InfoViewer` and `OutlinerItem`, so those exports render content only — never a "Delete polygon" / "Delete box" / trash button (FIT-2931).
- **Never discard unlabeled regions.** If nothing is selected in the LabelPicker the region is created with `labels: []`; relabel it later with `props.updateRegion(id, { labels, colors })` (always update `colors` with `labels`).
- **Hydrate with colors.** In `parseResults`, pass `{ labelColors }` into `from*Results` (or stamp `colors` afterward). The Regions panel has no `labelColors` fallback — empty `colors` means gray chips.
- **Do not show the in-canvas LayerManager.** `showLayers` defaults to false. Leave it off (and do not mount `*.LayerManager`) — the editor-shell Outliner / Regions panel is the region list. When the user asks for a region list in the Screen, build it with `RegionList` wired to the shell props (see the RegionList module), not `showLayers`.
- Pass the real frame rate: probe it with `EditorDeps.video.probeFrameRate` (see the video-timeline module) and hand the result to `frameRate`; do not assume 24.

```jsx
function TrackingScreen(props) {
  const VideoCanvas = window.InterfaceComponents.VideoCanvas;
  const LabelPicker = window.InterfaceComponents.LabelPicker;
  const [activeLabels, setActiveLabels] = React.useState(["Person"]);
  const [activeTimelineLabels, setActiveTimelineLabels] = React.useState(["Walking"]);
  return (
    <div>
      <LabelPicker labels={[{ value: "Person" }]} value={activeLabels}
        onChange={setActiveLabels} readOnly={props.readOnly} ariaLabel="Object labels" />
      <LabelPicker labels={[{ value: "Walking" }, { value: "Waiting" }]} value={activeTimelineLabels}
        onChange={setActiveTimelineLabels} readOnly={props.readOnly} ariaLabel="Activity labels" />
      <VideoCanvas
        src={getField(props.task.data, props.params?.videoField) || ""}
        frameRate={props.params?.frameRate || 25}
        regions={(props.regions || []).filter((r) => r._toName === "video")}
        selectedRegionIds={props.selectedRegionIds}
        activeLabels={activeLabels}
        activeTimelineLabels={activeTimelineLabels}
        labelColors={{ Person: "#2563eb", Walking: "#16836b", Waiting: "#9854cb" }}
        fromName="box"
        timelineFromName="activity"
        toName="video"
        enableTimelineLabels
        readOnly={props.readOnly}
        hotkeys={props.hotkeys}
        onAddRegion={props.addRegion}
        onUpdateRegion={props.updateRegion}
        onDeleteRegion={props.deleteRegion}
        onSelectRegion={(id, opts) => props.selectRegion(id, opts)}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

For custom layouts, compose `VideoCanvas.Toolbar`, `VideoCanvas.Viewport`, `VideoCanvas.TimelineControls`, `VideoCanvas.ObjectTimeline`, and `VideoCanvas.ActivityTimeline` inside the same `VideoCanvas.Root`. Render shared timeline controls once. All members use that root's playhead and timeline viewport. In a custom composition, conditionally render the members to control visibility; the root's showTimeline/showObjectTimeline/showActivityTimeline props configure only its default layout.

- Do NOT rebuild keyframes from `currentTime`; `_value.sequence` is authoritative and already frame-indexed.
- Do NOT create separate VideoCanvas roots for the two timeline panels; their controlled regions, playhead, zoom, and scrolling belong to one video.
